subject: africanElephant
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: adult African bush elephant.
Style: low-poly.
reasoning:
Looking at the renders, I'm checking the ear placement since they look like flat vertical plates sticking outward, and in the three-quarter view there seems to be an odd extra ear peeking above the head that needs fixing.

Legs look thin relative to the oversized rectangular body slab, and I want to make sure the trunk, with its heavy dark rings, connects naturally to the head and the tusks don't awkwardly intersect it. The skin texture also needs attention—the horizontal wrinkle lines read too much like wood grain and should be toned down, along with the overly dark mud coloring.

There's also a floating brown knob near the ear and a brow block that look detached rather than integrated into the face, so those need fixing or removing. The eye feels too small at roughly 0.23 width and should be bumped up to around 0.3, and the base the elephant sits on is oversized relative to the model, so I should shrink its radius to around 2.7 to better match the elephant's actual footprint.

The real priority though is the overall body shape: the top is too flat and needs a shoulder hump, head dome, and sagging back, plus a belly bulge, and the legs need to read as thick, straight columns rather than kinked limbs. Right now the legs taper with faceted bends from smooth:false, giving them an awkward pillar-with-kinks look — I want to adjust the leg radius profile to stay closer to 0.4 near the ground and remove the bend-induced kinks so they look like proper straight elephant legs.

Beyond that, I'm thinking about adding loft stations to shape the back hump and rump rounding, softening the wrinkle texture strength, and adjusting the ear orientation so they flare back more naturally instead of sitting like flat front-facing planks.

Skipping some minor details like eyelashes and gland streaks as unnecessary. I'm settling on key fixes: enlarging the eye and removing the protruding cheek knob blocks in favor of a flatter, more integrated brow shape.

Then I'll remove the brow stick entirely, shrink the cheek offset inward, thicken the legs, soften the wrinkle, and bump up the skull scale slightly larger while keeping the forehead dome in place, plus adjust the trunk rings.

Now I'm softening the wrinkle torus by making its color closer to skin tone and thinning it out, leaving the nostrils as they are. I'm also adding body shaping—a shoulder hump sphere near the top of the body and a rounded rump sphere lower down—to give the spine more natural contour.

Adjusting leg and foot proportions: widening the foot cylinder radii and shifting nail positions outward to match, plus softening the wrinkle blend intensity with a noise mask and slightly resizing the eye decal.

I'm also removing the brow-hit detection lines entirely, repositioning the cheek sphere closer to center with slightly larger scale, and tweaking the torus wrinkle geometry parameters.
